DIRECT TESTIMONY OF ASHLEY GULBRANSON

Respectfully submitted,
Ashley Gulbranson

By:	/s/ Ashley Gulbranson                        		

19901 Firefly Road
Florence, Texas 76527
Telephone: 512-639-3959
Email: eveninggraceessentials@yahoo.com

INTRODUCTION 
Q. PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME FOR THE RECORD. 
A. Ashley Gulbranson
Q. PLEASE STATE YOUR ADDRESS FOR THE RECORD. 
A. 19901 Firefly Road, Florence, Texas 76527
Q. DO ANY OF THE PROPOSED TRANSMISSION ROUTES IMPACT PROPERTY YOU OWN? 
	A. Yes
Q. LIST THE SPECIFIC ROUTE LINK(S) THAT IMPACT PROPERTY YOU OWN?
A. G71, G72 and G73

NOTICE AND PUBLIC MEETINGS
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE A NOTICE IN THE MAIL FROM THE APPLICANTS LAST SPRING ABOUT THE PROJECT AND THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC MEETINGS?
A. No, I did not.
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE A PACKET IN THE MAIL FROM THE APPLICANTS REGARDING THE PROPOSED TRANSMISSION LINE ROUTES?
A. Yes, I did.
Q. WHEN DID YOU RECEIVE THAT PACKET IN THE MAIL?
A. I received a packet in the mail Monday March 30, 2026.
Q. DID YOU RECEIVE ANY NOTIFICATION FROM THE APPLICANTS OR THE PUC ABOUT THE PROJECT PRIOR TO RECENT PACKET YOU RECEIVED IN THE MAIL IN APRIL 2026?
A. No, I did not.
Q. DO YOU KNOW WHY YOU DID NOT RECEIVE A NOTICE ABOUT THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC MEETINGS?
A. It is my understanding that route links G71, G72 and G73 were added after to the public meeting in June of 2025.

ATTEMPTS TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION  
Q. ONCE YOU RECEIVED YOUR NOTIFICATION, DID YOU ATTEMPT TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION?
A. Yes, I did.
Q. APPROXIMATELY HOW MANY LAW OFFICES THAT SPECIALIZE IN PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS LEGAL PROCEEDINGS DID YOU CONTACT IN AN ATTEMPT TO OBTAIN LEGAL REPRESENTATION?
A. I contacted approximately 10 law offices and legal professionals that specialize in Public Utility Commission proceedings and eminent domain matters.  
Q. OF THE SPECIALIZED LAW OFFICES YOU CONTACTED, HOW MANY WERE AVAILABLE TO TAKE YOU AS A CLIENT?
A. Of those that responded to me, none were available. Each one had conflicts of interest, most likely being the landowners who engaged them soon after the June 2025 Public Meetings. 
Q. IF A LAW OFFICE WITH SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE WOULD HAVE BEEN AVAILABLE TO ACCEPT YOU AS A CLIENT, WOULD YOU HAVE MOVED FORWARD WITH LEGAL REPRESENTATION?

A. Yes. Absolutely.  I would have immediately retained legal counsel that had specialized expertise in PUC transmission line projects, if representation had been available, either by myself or with a group of neighbors.

DUE PROCESS AND TIMELINE CONCERNS
Q. HAS THE CONSTRAINED TIMELINE RESULTING FROM ONCOR’S AND LCRA’S FAILURE TO NOTIFY YOU, AND AS IMPOSED BY THE SHORT 180-DAY TIMEFRAME FOR THESE PROCEEDINGS, COMBINED WITH THE LACK OF AVAILABLE LEGAL REPRESENTATION, HAMPERED YOUR ABILITY TO EFFECTIVELY NAVIGATE THE PROJECT AND LEGAL PROCEDURES AS IS NECESSARY TO EXERCISE YOUR RIGHTS OF DUE PROCESS?
	A. Yes. I am a homeschool mom of four. I have no prior knowledge to things like filing, preparing testimony, making motions, responding to the court, submitting evidence, briefs, and the list goes on and on. I have been given a very short time frame to learn and decipher a process that is completely new to me. This condensed timeline along with the inability to secure legal representation has greatly restricted my ability to properly understand, prepare for, and participate in these proceedings.
.
The requirements that are associated with the Public Utility Commission proceedings are ones that are completely unfamiliar to an ordinary landowner like myself. Unlike the Applicants, Commission Staff, and parties who routinely participate in these proceedings as their profession, we, as affected landowners, are attempting to defend our homes, our property rights, and our family’s future while simultaneously continuing daily in responsibilities, maintaining employment, and attending to family responsibilities. 
The condensed procedural schedule has greatly limited my ability to adequately understand requirements and filings, to prepare testimony, and participate in this process meaningfully. This situation was only made harder because many of the qualified attorneys familiar with Public Utility Commission litigation had already been retained by others involved in the proceeding, making legal representation unavailable to many landowners like me.
In my opinion, this whole process has created a significant disadvantage for us ordinary landowners, and it has hindered meaningful participation as well as due process protections that should be offered in proceedings of this consequence and significance.

Q. CURRENTLY, WHAT ARE YOUR BIGGEST STRUGGLES REGARDING THE PROJECT?
A. This propped transmission line will come within 300’ of our home. We are a homeschool family, making our home also our school. We own and run a small business from our home and building. Having this line so close to where my four young children spend all their time is concerning to me.

Q. WHAT IS THE WORST PART ABOUT THE CURRENT SITUATION? 
A. In my opinion, this is moving at an unneccessarily fast pace for such a large project. There has been extremely limited time to prepare. I’ve not had adequate time to learn how to properly defend my rights as a landowner. Myself and other landowners have not been able to find experienced lawyers who have not already been retained. There have been no PUC public meetings or workshops to assist us or educate us on the project.

Q. WHAT COULD HAVE OR SHOULD HAVE BEEN DONE DIFFERENTLY, IN YOUR OPINION?
A. In my opinion, myself and other landowners should have been notified of the new links earlier. Oncor and LCRA should have informed each of us when they had knowledge of a new route being added. We should have been offered a full public meeting after being notified just like those were given in June of 2025. I was not given the opportunity to ask questions. I was not given the chance to express my concerns. Myself and many other landowners were not given the opportunity to have a voice in this process equally to those who were given more notice. 

Q. IN YOUR OPINION, WHAT SHOULD BE DONE TO REPAIR THE DAMAGE DONE TO YOU BY NOT BEING NOTIFIED WHEN YOUR ROUTE WAS FIRST CONSIDERED, AS WAS DONE WITH THE ROUTE SHOWN AT THE JUNE 2025 HEARING?
	A. An additional public meeting should have been offered to myself, my neighbors and many landowners who were not offered the same due process others were afforded. In my opinion, I (along with all other landowners recently notified) should be offered more time in this process. I need time to give comments, like those at the June 2025 meeting were able to do. Oncor and LCRA also need time to review those comments and incorporate them into this process, much the same as they had to do with the comments provided by those who were properly notified in June. I need time to be able to provide Oncor and LCRA with information that is vital to their study of this area such as buildings and structures on our property. More time is what myself, my neighbors, and other affected landowners that were recently notified need. Oncor and LCRA have denied us of that opportunity.

Q. IN YOUR OPINION, IS THERE ANYTHING THAT CAN BE DONE NOW TO REMEDY YOUR LOSS OF DUE PROCESS?
A. Yes, there is. In my opinion, myself and all others directly impacted on the route links that were notified after the public meeting in June of 2025 should be given the same consideration those notified before that meeting were given. The PUC must determine how to correct the wrongdoing that has been carried out by Oncor and LCRA. The PUC should extend equal opportunity to myself, my neighbors and fellow landowners to adequetly prepare to participate in this process. They should restore the rights which were so carelessly stomped upon.

Q. DO YOU HAVE ANYTHING ELSE YOU WOULD LIKE TO PROVIDE THAT IS IMPORTANT TO LET THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION KNOW ABOUT YOUR LAND, YOUR FAMILY, OR THESE PROCEEDINGS?
	
A. As stated above, we are a homeschooling family who spend all of our days in a home
 that will be approximately 300’ from where this line is proposed to go. My children play

 in our creeks, ride horses all around our property, have built playhouses and treehouses 

among the cedar trees, planted gardens, and all plan to one day have homes on this

 land. My husband and I are not lavish or extravagant people. We own a small 

business and work hard for everything that we have. This land is what we have. It is our

 legacy to our children and hopefully future generations. It is where we plan to grow old.

 We try our hardest to help our neighbors and those in need. And we are raising our

 children to do the same. However, our family, our neighbors, and many many others in 

this beautiful stretch of rural Texas have not been shown that same curtesy. We have 

been pushed into a situation that is moving at warp speed. While others were granted 

months, we were given mere weeks. While others had the opportunity to seek expert legal

 representation, we have been left scrambling to sort out a legal process we know nothing 

about on our own. We should be granted more time.
	

Q.  DO YOU HAVE A FINAL REQUEST? 
A. Yes. Please deny Oncor’s and LCRA’s request for CCN on the 59475 Bell County East 

to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line for knowingly withholding notice and failing to

 properly and adequately notify hundreds of directly impacted property owners.

Q. DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY? 
	A. Yes
